outcome: Stop reporting silence before a selected audio track's first samples as decoded audio, and cite only probe evidence the repository carries.
criteria: A transcription request that begins before the selected track's first samples reads from that track's start, so no synthesized leading silence is counted as decoded audio.
A requested interval lying entirely before the selected track's first samples is refused as unread, naming the track and its start, instead of returning silence.
The perception README and the audio tool instructions describe the decoded interval at both ends and cite no evidence at a path the repository does not carry.
Focused regressions cover the clamped start, the new refusal and the absence of leading padding in real audio, and the full test suite passes.

dispositions.note: A request opening before the selected track now reports clip_start_s at the track's first samples; a real delayed-track read carries no leading synthesized silence.
An interval wholly before the track is refused, naming the track, its start and the readable interval, and runs no ASR.
The README and audio tool instructions describe both decoded endpoints, and the probe evidence is no longer cited at a gitignored path.
Synthetic and real-FFmpeg regressions cover the clamped start, the refusal and the absence of leading padding; 271 tests pass with no skips.

note: Reviewing 2026-09-10-0911-ppn6 left three residual points; two were real and are fixed here. Silence synthesized ahead of a track's first packet was returned as decoded audio, and a request lying wholly before the track returned nothing but silence under a success status, which is the failure its endpoint fix removed surviving at the head. Reading now begins at the track's own samples and an entirely earlier interval is refused. The third point, subprocess stdin isolation, was measured rather than changed: ffprobe never reads stdin and the ffmpeg calls already passed -nostdin, so the DEVNULL change hardens a latent path rather than fixing a live defect, and needs no further work. The new cache assertion surfaced a separate defect: max() and min() returned the caller's int on ties, so start_s=3 and start_s=3.0 addressed different cached transcripts; both endpoints are now floats. One existing real-media assertion encoded the old head padding and was changed deliberately to the new behaviour. No backend, scenario or seeking code was touched, and no benchmark score or ASR accuracy was remeasured.
